analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition in docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 413): a new row for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP. The row describes a load-time shape warmup for ordinary EngineV2 slots. The rollback values are 0/false/no/off and `always` skips the probe. The row says a 128-token shader-cache probe runs twice, only a cold cache runs shape cells, with a 20-second cap per engine, and that it trains no rate or counter. It also says the variable is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. I examined both supplied units (the full document text) and found no source or code change, so no security control changes in this PR.

Threat-model relevance: this is an availability/performance knob (TB-007, T-029, T-010 are adjacent) with a bounded 20-second warmup. It does not touch attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011), encryption, the prefix cache at-rest posture (T-041), or key handling. Warmup runs on synthetic shapes, so I see no consumer-prompt exposure from the doc. The prefix cache TTL, HMAC naming and kill-switch statements in the doc are unchanged. They remain consistent with T-041 (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 disables the SSD tier; the 30-minute TTL is not mentioned as changed).

Open integration questions, which are not findings because the implementation is outside the supplied evidence: (1) whether ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmupMode actually enforces the 20-second bound and uses only synthetic inputs; (2) whether the warmup probe could affect timing observable by consumers; (3) whether adding the variable to the LaunchAgent passthrough allowlist is implemented in LaunchAgent.swift as the doc states. The doc's claims are unverified against code, but no concrete regression is evidenced.
